name: truthstone
description: Deterministic, LLM-free reliability layer for Codex. By default it checks what a request takes for granted against the repository, denies irreversible commands until you approve them, and holds a 'done' that the recorded test evidence contradicts. Everything else it checks is recorded, not shown.

interface.longDescription:
Truthstone (previously named AgentGuard) sits beside Codex through lifecycle hooks and checks what the agent is about to do against the repository itself. By default it speaks in a few cases only: when a request relies on something the repository does not have (it tells Codex at the prompt and holds the first edit once); when a request that keeps the tests asks for a failing test to pass (it quotes the documented rule closest to the request); before an irreversible shell command (denied until you approve it with the code it gives); and at a 'done' that the recorded evidence contradicts, such as relevant tests that fail while the message does not say so, or tests that were weakened or skipped (the turn is held once). It also adds a short reminder at the first prompt of each session. When it speaks, it hands its evidence back to Codex, so the agent's own reasoning can fix the problem. Everything else it checks is recorded, not shown. With profile = "full" in ~/.truthstone/config.toml it also challenges code the repository does not have and edits far outside the task, and holds a finished turn that ran no tests.

It has no model of its own and makes no network calls while it works: everything runs in a local daemon on 127.0.0.1, with decisions recorded under ~/.truthstone. It never grants permissions — it can only stay silent, object, or ask for your confirmation — and if it is unavailable Codex simply continues unguarded. It works only inside git repositories; elsewhere its hooks do nothing.

Requires the Truthstone runtime (Python 3.12+). If it is not installed, the plugin installs a private copy with uv on first use, from the GitHub release that matches the plugin, or tells you how to install it; set TRUTHSTONE_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1 to skip that download. Codex runs plugin hooks only after you review and trust them in /hooks. Works in the Codex CLI and in local threads of the ChatGPT desktop app; hooks do not run in the IDE extension, web, mobile or cloud tasks.
defaultPrompt: Explain why Truthstone blocked my last action and how to resolve it
Check whether Truthstone is guarding this repository and fix the setup
Summarize what Truthstone has caught in this project this week
